proposals.objective: Add a wall-time excursion rule to the monitor: flag any run beyond 10 times its solver's running 99th percentile, stop and investigate beyond 100 times
proposals.rationale: Mined from the mega-batch ledger: solver wall times are tightly banded, with the cylinder at median 3.7 seconds and 99th percentile 19.7 seconds and the wing at median 5.8 seconds and 99th percentile 8.6 seconds, yet three runs per solver recorded wall times near 16300 seconds, over 800 times the 99th percentile, and every one was recorded ok with no anomaly anywhere. A hung or starved run that eventually returns a plausible number is invisible to every current check. The rule keeps the excursion as a named field on the record so fleet learning can separate solver cost from infrastructure stalls.
citations: Certonomous Mega-Batch Ledger, 39442 Rows Examined 2026-07-25
Certonomous Monitor Standard, Version 1.0
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The fleet ledger stops silently absorbing 800-fold wall-time excursions, and the cost model behind mission planning stops being polluted by infrastructure stalls counted as solver time

proposals.objective: Add residual-stall, oscillatory-divergence, and Courant-excursion rules to the monitor, covering the calm failure modes the spike rule cannot see
proposals.rationale: The lab's own evidence documents a failure the current monitor misses by design: the Re 200 cylinder stalls at residual near 1e-3 with a small force oscillation and exits on the iteration cap looking calm, because a steady solver applied past its regime degrades measurably but never spikes. Detection rules from the monitor standard: a stall is a rolling-median residual improving by less than a factor of 2 over 200 iterations while still above the residualControl target; oscillatory divergence is alternating-sign residual changes with a growing envelope over 50 iterations; a Courant excursion is the reported maximum exceeding the case limit or growing monotonically over 20 steps. A stalled result is UNCONVERGED no matter how smooth its tail, and the prescribed action is the regime check before any rerun buys more iterations. The Courant rule is written now so the first transient run arrives born monitored.
citations: Certonomous Numericist Knowledge Base, Validated Facts 3 And 4
Certonomous Monitor Standard, Version 1.0
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The monitor recognizes the graceful-degradation family of failures, so a run that exits on its iteration cap can never be mistaken for evidence again

proposals.objective: Back each fidelity chip with a compact credibility scorecard covering the two factors the chips do not encode: input pedigree and results robustness
proposals.rationale: Mapping the lab's four chips onto the NASA standard's assessment factors shows the chips already encode validation status, solver backing, and convergence. Two factors are invisible: input pedigree, so a run on poorly traced inputs can wear the same chip as one on measured inputs, and results robustness, so sensitivity knowledge never reaches the certificate. A per-result scorecard with a 0 to 4 level for each factor, following the standard's level definitions, closes the gap without changing what any chip means. The Womersley screening cap already behaves like the standard's placard requirement for use outside the validated domain, naming the limit, its extent, and the consequences; the scorecard states that explicitly. This is a content addition and may land directly on the certificate surfaces.
citations: NASA-STD-7009B, Standard For Models And Simulations, NASA 2024
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Every certificate states how well its inputs are traced and how well its sensitivities are known, in the same leveled language NASA uses for simulation credibility

proposals.objective: Label every case in the lab with its validation-hierarchy tier so the trust a result may carry is bounded by its tier on the record
proposals.rationale: Oberkampf and Trucano organize validation as a building-block hierarchy: unit problems, benchmark cases, subsystem cases, complete system, with experimental information degrading radically up the tiers. The lab's portfolio maps cleanly: the laminar cylinder is a unit problem, the TMR flat plate and the motorcycle are benchmark cases, the valve screen is a subsystem case, the airliner is the complete-system posture where data are scarcest. proposals.objective: Add a Sobol sensitivity mission type that apportions output variance across the input spreads before any uncertainty reduction campaign is priced
proposals.rationale: The lab propagates input spreads through Monte Carlo but never says which input owns the variance, so reduction work is untargeted. Variance-based decomposition gives main and total effect indices per input; on the reduced-order paths an evaluation costs about a millisecond, so a pick-and-freeze design of N times (M plus 2) evaluations at N of 200 is seconds of compute for the valve and comparable for the airliner surrogate. The mission ends with a ranking of inputs by variance share and a recommendation of where the next samples or the next measurement effort should go.
citations: Dakota Theory Manual, Stochastic Expansion Methods, Sandia National Laboratories
Dakota Reference Manual, Sampling With Variance Based Decomposition, Sandia National Laboratories
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Main and total effect Sobol indices for the valve inputs (flow amplitude 5 percent, discharge coefficient 6 percent) and the airliner inputs (span, area, sweep, taper), plus a standing answer to which spread is worth buying down first
proposals.launch_prompt: Run a Sobol sensitivity mission on the valve screen: inputs are flow amplitude (sigma 5 percent) and discharge coefficient (sigma 6 percent); evaluate the cycle-weighted loss through the reduced-order orifice path with a pick-and-freeze design, N 200, cost N times (M plus 2) equals 800 evaluations; report main and total effect indices with bootstrap confidence intervals, then repeat on the airliner input spreads through the fitted surrogate with one confirming solver run at the highest-index corner. Present the result as a variance-share bar per input with the earned-badge convention.

proposals.objective: Adopt a multifidelity Monte Carlo propagation scheme that fuses the reduced-order ensemble with a few anchoring solver evaluations instead of racing them
proposals.rationale: The race act already produces the exact data multifidelity fusion needs: the same designs evaluated through the reduced-order lane and the solver lane. Multifidelity Monte Carlo is an unbiased control-variate estimator; the measured correlation between the paired lanes and the measured cost ratio decide the optimal sample allocation analytically, and also decide honestly whether fusion pays at all. Today the pairing is discarded once the race ends. The scheme keeps the solver in the loop for the accuracy guarantee, uses the reduced-order ensemble for volume, and reports one fused envelope with the correlation and allocation on the record.
citations: Survey Of Multifidelity Methods In Uncertainty Propagation, Inference, And Optimization, Peherstorfer, Willcox And Gunzburger, SIAM Review 2018
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The measured correlation between the reduced-order lane and the solver lane on a shared design set, the resulting optimal allocation, and a fused envelope whose variance undercuts the solver-only estimate at equal budget or is honestly reported as not paying
proposals.launch_prompt: On the race act design space, take the paired records where both lanes evaluated the same design, measure the correlation and the cost ratio, compute the optimal multifidelity Monte Carlo allocation and control-variate coefficient, then run the fused estimator at the same core-minute budget as the solver-only lane and report both envelopes side by side with the allocation stated.

proposals.objective: Give the model channel a measured parametric basis: propagate published k-omega SST closure-coefficient intervals through solves on the motorcycle held mesh and report the resulting drag envelope as coefficient-interval evidence alongside the current transferred estimate
proposals.rationale: The model channel today rests on closure-family spread and validation-history transfer; neither measures how much of the answer rides on the closure coefficients themselves. The Schaefer papers supply defensible epistemic intervals with named provenance for every SST coefficient (beta-star in [0.0784, 0.1024] from Wilcox's measured stress ratio, a1 in [0.31, 0.40] which may only be increased, kappa in [0.38, 0.42] from pipe-flow experiments) and show SST is the most coefficient-sensitive of the common RANS models, with beta-star dominating drag and skin friction and a1 rising wherever the flow separates - directly relevant to a bluff body carrying a rider. The recipe holds the 353,578-cell motorcycle mesh and numerics fixed, restarts each case from the converged baseline (the papers' own cost trick), and solves one-at-a-time corner cases for the five coefficients the papers found significant: beta-star, a1, sigma-w1, beta-star/beta1, beta-star/beta2, each at its interval bounds with a1 varied upward only. Ten solves at about six minutes each from measured motorcycle solve times gives roughly 60 core-minutes; the drag envelope across the set is a measured coefficient-interval band, reported as an interval (no probability density assumed), never folded into the quadrature u_val as a sigma. If the band is material against the numerical channel of plus or minus 0.00053 on Cd, a second stage promotes the top three coefficients to a 20-sample Latin Hypercube set (order-2 response surface at oversampling 2, per the papers' design) and runs the new Sobol analysis layer for variance shares, about 120 further core-minutes. Caveat carried honestly: the intervals' provenance is flow-independent but the papers' sensitivity rankings are transonic; our solves measure the incompressible separated-flow ranking locally, which is the point.
citations: Uncertainty Quantification of Turbulence Model Closure Coefficients for Transonic Wall-Bounded Flows, Schaefer, Hosder, West, Rumsey, Carlson and Kleb, AIAA Journal 55(1), 2017
Uncertainty Quantification and Sensitivity Analysis of SA Turbulence Model Coefficients in Two and Three Dimensions, Schaefer, Cary, Mani and Spalart, AIAA 2017-1710
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: A measured coefficient-interval band on the motorcycle Cd for the model channel, a ranking of the five SST coefficients by drag swing in an incompressible separated flow (testing whether the papers' transonic ranking of beta-star first and a1-in-separation transfers), and a standing perturbed-coefficient recipe reusable on any held mesh
proposals.launch_prompt: Run a closure-coefficient uncertainty mission on the motorcycle held mesh: hold mesh and numerics fixed, restart every case from the converged baseline, and solve one-at-a-time corner cases for the five significant SST coefficients - beta-star in [0.0784, 0.1024], a1 in [0.31, 0.40] upward only, sigma-w1 in [0.3, 0.7], beta-star/beta1 in [1.19, 1.31], beta-star/beta2 in [1.05, 1.45] - ten solves at about six minutes each. Report the Cd envelope across the set as the measured coefficient-interval band for the model channel, shown alongside (not replacing) the transferred estimate and stated as an interval, and rank the coefficients by swing. If the band is material against the numerical channel, promote the top three coefficients to a 20-sample Latin Hypercube set and run the Sobol analysis layer for variance shares with the earned-badge convention.
